explain.say: In the first pages we learn that Okonkwo became famous across nine villages by throwing an unbeaten wrestler. Chinua Achebe published Things Fall Apart in 1958, two years before Nigeria's independence, and it became the most widely read African novel. A gentle note: it includes the killing of a child and a suicide. The panels follow Okonkwo's life.

explain.say: Achebe's first aim was to show that Igbo society had its own rich order before Europeans came. Sort what holds Umuofia together: a court where masked ancestral spirits judge disputes, a personal god called a chi, titles earned by hard work, and yams, the king of crops. Why would showing this matter so much in 1958?

Look at the third panel, the hardest moment. Ikemefuna, a boy given to Umuofia to settle a dispute, lives with Okonkwo's family for three years and calls him father. When the Oracle decrees the boy must die, Okonkwo, afraid of looking weak, strikes the final blow. How does fear of weakness make him cruel?

explain.say: Part three brings missionaries, then colonial government. On the left, the village as it was; on the right, what arrives: a church, a court and a prison. Okonkwo's son Nwoye, troubled by Ikemefuna's death, joins the church. Achebe shows change came from inside as well as outside. Why might some villagers welcome the new religion?

Okonkwo kills a court messenger, but the clan will not rise with him, and he hangs himself, a deep offence against the earth. The British District Commissioner thinks his story might fill a paragraph in a book about pacifying the tribes. Superb thinking. Challenge: why does Achebe end with the colonizer's view?

faq.a: When his clan will not fight the colonisers after he kills a messenger, Okonkwo sees that the world he lived for has gone. Suicide is an abomination in Igbo belief, so his end shows how completely things have fallen apart.
asks: How does Things Fall Apart end?

faq.q: Why did Achebe write Things Fall Apart?
faq.a: Partly to answer European novels, such as Joyce Cary's Mister Johnson and Conrad's Heart of Darkness, that showed Africans without history or dignity. He wanted to show a complex Igbo society from the inside, flaws included.
A boy handed to Umuofia by a neighbouring village as compensation for a killing. He lives with Okonkwo for three years and loves him, but the Oracle orders his death and Okonkwo takes part.
Okonkwo's father, a gentle, music-loving man who died in debt. Okonkwo's whole life is driven by fear of being like him.

faq.q: Why does Nwoye convert to Christianity?
faq.a: He is disturbed by the killing of Ikemefuna and the abandonment of twins, and the hymns of the missionaries answer questions his father's world could not. He takes the name Isaac.

facts: Things Fall Apart was published in London in 1958.
The title comes from W. B. Yeats's poem The Second Coming.
It has been translated into more than fifty languages.
